title: Add modular RAG playbook mini-lab with stepwise validation and portable fixtures
author: Lena Fischer
release_notes: Introduces a compact, modular RAG mini-lab quickstart that demonstrates stepwise validation, portable fixtures, and telemetry probes for authors and platform engineers.
description:
Summary: This PR adds a compact, modular RAG playbook mini-lab intended for developer onboarding and local experimentation. The goal is to provide a self-contained walk-through that demonstrates: 1) a minimal retrieval pipeline and index format, 2) stepwise assertion-driven validation for outputs, 3) portable fixtures that can be swapped for real corpora or local mocks, and 4) lightweight telemetry probes so authors can see latency/cost breakdowns for prompts and retrievals.
Motivation: new developer flows keep showing the same setup overhead (indexing, fixtures, test harness). This quickstart removes that friction with a deterministic mini-lab that maps directly to Redwood Optimize and Console telemetry hooks.
Checklist:
- [x] Add modular playbook and README with step-by-step run instructions
- [x] Provide sample fixtures (index + short doc set) and a shimbed local indexer
- [x] Implement a stepwise validation harness (assertion-driven)
- [x] Wire telemetry probes and local console shim
- [x] Add CI smoke test that runs playbook end-to-end (fast mode)
- [x] Update docs site index and quickstart registry
Changes (high level):
- quickstarts/rag-mini-lab/README.md: user-facing walkthrough, goals, and troubleshooting tips
- quickstarts/rag-mini-lab/playbook.yaml: canonical playbook manifest with named steps and contract expectations
- quickstarts/rag-mini-lab/fixtures/sample-index.jsonl: small, portable index snapshot used by the mini-lab
- quickstarts/rag-mini-lab/fixtures/sample-corpus/*.md: three short documents used for retrieval
- quickstarts/rag-mini-lab/harness/validate.py: assertion harness that runs each step and records pass/fail
- quickstarts/rag-mini-lab/telemetry/probes.yaml: docker-friendly probe config that emits timing and token-cost estimates
- scripts/run-local.sh: convenience script to run the mini-lab in a dev container
- .github/workflows/quickstart-ci.yml: CI job to run the playbook in headless fast mode
Commits (summary):
- c1a7b2d: initial scaffold with playbook manifest, README and fixtures
- 8e3f4a1: add validation harness and telemetry probe config; basic smoke runner
- 2b9cab3: CI integration and lint fixes
- f6d4e9a: address reviewer feedback on credential handling and env defaults
Notable snippets (illustrative only):
- playbook step example: "steps:\n  - id: retrieve\n    action: fetch_docs\n    expects: '>=1'"
- validation assertion example from harness: "assert len(retrieved) >= 1, 'no docs returned'"
Review conversation (high level):
- Owen Park (reviewer): "Love the compact approach. Two asks: make the fixtures optional via env var and add a note about production index formats in the README."
- Lena (author): "Added QUICKSTART_USE_FIXTURES=false support and extended README with a short section linking to model-registry and index-format notes."
- Asha Patel (reviewer): "CI flaked on the smoke run initially — looks like the local container sometimes fails to download base images in the runner. Suggest caching or using a smaller base image."
- Lena (author): "Switched to alpine-slim base for the smoke runner and added a retry loop for container pulls. Re-ran CI and verified stable runs."
- Miguel Torres (reviewer): "Telemetry probe wording: call out that values are estimates and reference Console docs for token accounting."
- Lena (author): "Clarified wording and added link to docs site section (docs/telemetry/token-accounting)."
CI details:
- Initial run: lint passed, unit tests passed, quickstart smoke failed (timeout pulling images)
- Fixes: reduced base image size and added retry, re-run succeeded
- CI checks (final): lint/pass, unit tests/pass, quickstart-smoke/pass, docs-build/pass
Merge outcome: merged via squash and merge on 2026-02-20.
Backported: none (no production code affected).
Testing instructions for maintainers:
1) Clone repo, cd quickstarts/rag-mini-lab
2) ./scripts/run-local.sh --fast (runs headless, uses fixtures)
3) For a full experiment: ./scripts/run-local.sh (will build dev container and run playbook)
4) Validate results in harness/output/{timestamp}.json (contains step pass/fail and probe timings)
Telemetry and cost notes: The telemetry probes are intentionally conservative and use token-estimates; they are meant for learning and not billing. We surface probe outputs as JSON artifacts so authors can iterate on prompts and retrieval strategies quickly.
Security and secrets: The quickstart is explicitly credential-optional; by default it uses fixtures. If you supply REAL_RETRIEVAL_ENDPOINT and API_KEY env vars the playbook will route calls to your configured retrieval service. I added guardrails to avoid accidental credential leaks in logs.
Docs changes: small docs site index entry added under /quickstarts with a short blurb and a link to the lab.
Related linear items: ENG-1289 (authoring mini-lab), PM-402 (quickstart discoverability).
Files changed count: 8.
Impact: Improves time-to-first-success for authors evaluating RAG workflows and provides a portable, testable template for building stepwise RAG quickstarts. If issues are found post-merge, create a follow-up PR referencing ENG-1289.
